notes: Source is US 6,115,188 ("Optical system and optical apparatus having the same", Canon Inc / Canon Kabushiki Kaisha, inventors Akihiro Nishio, Hideki Ogawa, Makoto Misaka; priority 10/16/1997 (JP2-9957397A) + 2 more JP priorities, filed 10/14/1998, published/granted 9/5/2000). This is an image-stabilized (IS) optical-system patent with 16 numerical examples spanning several focal-length classes (approx. 294, 392, 490 and 589 mm); Numerical Example 1 (f=293.58, Fno=2.9, 2w=8.4deg) is used here for the 300 mm slot. The SAME patent's Numerical Examples 7 and 10 are used for the 400 mm and 500 mm slots in this set (data/lenses/p400.json, p500.json), so the three share one design lineage and one inner-focus/IS architecture -- documented together in research/lenses-tele.md.

The patent's own text: 'Next, sixteen numerical examples 1 to 16 of the first embodiment are shown... In the numerical examples 1 to 7 and 9 to 16, the last two surfaces define a glass block such as phase plate or filter.' For Example 1 that is the last two rows (R28, R29): transcribed here as the filter (glass, nd=1.51633, vd=64.1) plus its rear flat surface. IMPORTANT SELF-CHECK FINDING: the patent prints the very last row as 'D29 = 0.00' and gives NO separate 'Bf=' label anywhere in the patent (grepped the full text for 'Bf', 'back focal', 'total length' -- only found in unrelated prose about design conditions, never a numeric value). Reading D29=0.00 as a literal stated Bf was tried first and FAILED the self-check badly (computed BF = 59.32 mm vs assumed-stated 0.00 mm, off by 59 mm) while EFL matched to +0.007% -- since EFL depends on the exact same r/t/n data as BF, this means the transcription is correct and D29=0.000 is simply a table-terminator formatting convention in this patent (all 16 examples end their row this way), not a real physical claim. The last surface's t here is therefore DERIVED from our own paraxial trace (59.32 mm), not patent-stated, and stated.bf is left out of the JSON's PatentStated block accordingly. This same issue and fix applies to p400.json and p500.json (Numerical Examples 7 and 10 of the same patent).

Aperture stop: printed explicitly in the raw table as 'R14 = Stop', so (unlike the 200 mm Nikon lens) this position is NOT a guess. Represented here as its own flat (r=null), zero-power surface at index 13 (0-based), matching the patent's own row.

Focus: the patent's description states focusing is done by 'axially moving the second lens unit L2 toward the image side... when the object distance decreases from infinity to a minimum' -- an inner-focus design (focus.method='inner'). However, THIS numerical example's table gives only the infinity-focus D values; no close-focus variable-gap distance is printed for Example 1 (contrast with the Nikon 200 mm patent, which does print D0/d11/d16 at both infinity and near focus). No VariableGap entries are recorded here as a result -- fabricating one would violate the 'never invent a number' rule.

Elements/groups counted directly from the cemented-interface pattern (zero air gap, glass on both sides of a shared surface = cemented group): front group L1 = 5 singlets (5 groups); L2 = 1 cemented doublet (1 group, the inner-focus group); rear group L3 = 4 doublets... actually 2 doublets + 1 singlet + 1 doublet = let's just state the count: (L3a doublet)+(L3b doublet)+(L3c singlet)+(L3d doublet) = 4 groups, 7 elements. Total: 5+1+7 = 13 real lens elements + 1 filter block = 15 counted here (elements field includes the filter, since lens-types.ts does not explicitly exclude it); groups = 5+1+4 = 10 lens groups + 1 filter group + 1 fixed-stop-adjacent air gap (not a group) -- recorded as groups=12 to include the filter as its own group, consistent with 'elements' also including it. This is a plain count from the prescription, not a claim about any commercial product's published spec.

No effective/clear diameters are printed anywhere in this patent for any of its 16 numerical examples, so every sd here is sdSource='estimated-from-marginal-ray' via .local/lens-tele/paraxial.py, using the same method as the 200 mm lens: entrance-beam semi-diameter at surface 1 set to EFL_computed/(2*Fno_stated), traced forward, plus the paraxial chief ray at the patent's OWN printed half field (2w=8.4deg / 2 = 4.2deg, so no assumption needed here, unlike the 200mm lens). See research/lenses-tele.md for the printed self-check numbers.

representativeOf intentionally left unset: no public source found that ties US 6,115,188 to a specific commercial Canon product, despite the strong circumstantial match (focal-length classes, Fno classes and 1998 filing date all line up with Canon's original EF 300/400/500/600mm f/2.8-4L IS USM lenses launched in 1999).
Lead 9/28/2026: elements/groups (15/11, was 15/12) count lens elements only; the drop-in filter plate is marked plate: "drop-in-filter" and is not an element or a group.
